note: THE THINGS NO SCRIPT CAN FIND. Everything an audit can detect belongs in an audit, not here - a hand-written ticket for 'these entries are thin' would go stale while audit-entry-depth.mjs finds the same thing every run and stops finding it the moment it is fixed. This file holds only what a script cannot know: work that needs Rob specifically, dates to watch for, and decisions already taken so they do not get relitigated.
howToUse: npm run worklist prints it. It is also printed at the end of npm run audit:weekly, so the human items sit beside the machine ones. Add entries by editing this file - keep them short, and delete blockedOnRob and watch entries when they are done rather than marking them complete. `decided` is the exception: append-only, because its whole purpose is to answer 'why is it like this' six months from now.

watch.what: Reddit's own JSON 403s curl and the /last30days engine 429s after ~14 items. arctic-shift works but rate-limits silently - an unthrottled sweep returned zero for 11 of 15 subreddits and looked like an empty window. Throttle and run in the background; ~30 minutes for 15 subs.

telegraph.co.uk answers every user agent with HTTP 402 and "not authorized without a valid TollBit Token" - paid bot licensing. It is seeded in six hotel corpora and contributes nothing to any of them. Not fixable and not to be worked around; left in the files so the refusal stays visible.
allaroundlondon.com began 403ing every path including its sitemap during the 9 Sept 2026 pass. It carries the Soho corpus, so that corpus has degraded since it was built.

The Distillery, Notting Hill has closed - the-distillery.london now redirects to a Shopify gin shop and the Ginstitute has moved to The Portobello Star. It is still being named by 2026 guides off a stale Tripadvisor entry, so it will keep reappearing in the corpus. Not on our sheet; recorded so nobody adds it.

Montcalm Mayfair was The Montcalm Marble Arch; The Carlton Tower is now Jumeirah Carlton Tower; The Henrietta is now Henrietta Experimental (and carries 4 domains once the variants merge, not 2); The Tower Hotel now trades as The Tower Hotel by Thistle; Four Seasons Ten Trinity Square became Four Seasons at Tower Bridge in Oct 2024; No.5 Maddox Street now sells serviced apartments, not hotel rooms; citizenM has been bought by Marriott and citizenm.com redirects to marriott.com.

Four independent travellers in the community pass recommended university rooms let over the summer - LSE Bankside House, Passfield Hall, Imperial, and UniversityRooms.com as the aggregator. We have no coverage of this at all and it is a genuine budget-accommodation category, not a hostel.

Reddit repeatedly asserts Onefam refuses over-35s and argues about it at length. Nobody quotes a policy. Onefam's own FAQ mentions age-specific DISCOUNTS and states no restriction. Do not repeat the claim without the operator confirming it.

Also, both "Is Palmers Lodge the best hostel in London?" threads are one blogger crossposting their own sidestreetstyle.com article - a genuine stay, but self-promotion, and Palmers Lodge is now a sheet row on five guide domains rather than on that.

decided.decision: Souk states '100% Halal HMC certified' on its own FAQ and is not on HMC's published register. Do not print the discrepancy; file the venue under the kitchen's own word.
decided.why: A published claim about a real business, with innocent explanations available - certification lapses and is renewed, registers lag. The finding stays in data/topics/halal.json under theSoukProblem, and verify-halal-citations.mjs enforces the decision in both directions.

decided.decision: Only link a hotel where the reader is plausibly being told where to stay. Five mentions are deliberately unlinked: a bar's address, a mural's wall, a restaurant inside a hotel, a hotel explicitly described as open to non-residents, and an exclusion list of places that are NOT pod hotels.
decided.why: Chasing full coverage would have put affiliate links on sentences that are not recommendations, which is what makes disclosure meaningless.

decided.decision: Monthly guides split into data/months/<month>.json (annual fixtures as date RULES) and <month>-<year>.json (that year's specifics). The annual refresh is an overlay refill, not a rewrite.
decided.why: Twelve guides on an annual cycle is twelve rewrites a year otherwise. The Christmas guide shows the failure mode - 2026 dates woven through prose.

decided.decision: Monthly guides carry a curated handful of gigs, never full listings.
decided.why: Rob's call. Comprehensive listings are a losing fight against Songkick and DICE; a short list worth planning a trip around is something they do not do.

decided.decision: An area guide's Where to stay section keeps its own sub-area prose (never a hotel list - AreaHotels already renders those from the sheet) and closes with a benefit-led link naming what the deep dive adds. The deep dive links back once.
decided.why: Established by the Shoreditch pair. A bare 'read more' does not earn the click; the specifics do.

decided.decision: No ticket tracker. Anything a script can detect stays in an audit; this file holds only what a script cannot know.
decided.why: A hand-written ticket for 'these entries are thin' goes stale and needs closing by hand. audit-entry-depth.mjs found eight thin Shoreditch entries nobody had noticed and will stop reporting them the moment they are fixed.

decided.decision: data/closed-hotels.json is the stop for a closed or renamed property. remark-hotel-links.mjs degrades a closed slug to plain text and warns; AreaHotels.astro keeps the card but swaps the booking link for the closure note.
decided.why: hotels.json is generated from the sheet and carries no status field, so nothing could stop the site selling a hotel that had shut. Clink 78 closed until 2027 and kings-cross-area-guide went on rendering a paid Check prices link to it. Keeping the card and saying it is closed beats deleting it - a reader who has heard of the place gets an answer.

decided.decision: src/data/hotels.json is a curated shortlist of what we can recommend and link - about 125 rows, 63 linkable - not an inventory of London hotels. Never make an absence claim about an area from it, never print a count of our rows as a count of the area's hotels, and name properties with no row in prose without a hotel: link where they belong. Every agent brief for a hotel or where-to-stay guide must carry this.
decided.why: Rob, 2026-09-09. The Soho and Covent Garden guides both claimed an area sold nothing between two price points; Soho's rested on seven of our own rows and Covent Garden's on six, and neither was a survey. The claim was also wrong inside our own data - the one property genuinely rate-sampled reached £466 and £901 on the same dates the gap was said to start at £287. Prices are typicalFrom estimates unless the slug is in src/data/hotel-rate-ranges.json, which covers only eight properties.

decided.what: namedBy counts distinct DOMAINS, not pages or corpora. A blog with five accommodation pages is one voice; four sources in one corpus is a consensus, one source in each of four corpora is one magazine house style.
decided.why: Love and London's five pages each scored as a separate source and briefly promoted her byline and a photo caption to four-source candidates.

decided.what: Fifteen domains excluded from the hotel corpora as AI SEO farms or template aggregators, listed in every data/serp/hotels-*.txt header and explained in data/reference/hotel-corpus.md.
decided.why: lamplitlondon.com ranked in five of the eight area searches and its name arrays are clean and correct. You cannot detect a farm from its output - you have to look at the site.

decided.what: SECTION_LABEL gained the hotel-domain plurals and a LOGISTICS_HEADING filter; collect() now splits on a pipe as well as a spaced dash.
decided.why: Section headings like "Grand Luxury Hotels" and "The Tube" counted as venues, took the surviving-heading count over the fallback gate, and stopped the <strong> harvest running - Santorini Dave appears in six corpora and was contributing nothing. Separately, a " | Area" suffix pushed long hotel names past isHeadline's nine-word limit and deleted them.
